meta.title: Foreign Buyer's Guide | Rui Da Cruz
meta.description: A general guide to buying property in Portugal as an international buyer — NIF, the purchase process, timelines and costs.

guiaCompradorEstrangeiro.title: Foreign Buyer's Guide
guiaCompradorEstrangeiro.intro: Buying property in Portugal as a non-resident follows a well-defined process. This guide summarises the main steps — it does not replace personalised legal or tax advice.

sections.title: Residency and NIF
sections.body: The first practical step is obtaining a Portuguese Tax Identification Number (NIF), required to open a bank account, sign contracts and pay taxes in Portugal. Depending on your nationality and goals, it may also be worth exploring the residency routes available — we recommend speaking with an immigration lawyer to understand which applies to your situation.

sections.title: The Purchase Process
sections.body: Once you have chosen a property, the process typically follows these steps: due diligence on the property (Land Registry Certificate and Tax Registration Document), signing the Promissory Purchase and Sale Contract (CPCV) with a deposit, and finally the Public Deed before a notary, followed by the final registration of the property in your name.

sections.title: Timelines and Costs
sections.body: The time between the CPCV and the deed varies — usually a few weeks to a few months, mostly depending on financing. Beyond the purchase price, there are taxes and fees to consider (such as IMT and Stamp Duty, among other notary and registry costs) — your lawyer or accountant in Portugal can calculate the exact amount for your case.

guiaCompradorEstrangeiro.disclaimer: This guide is informational and general in nature — it does not replace personalised legal, tax or financial advice. We always recommend consulting a lawyer or accountant licensed in Portugal before proceeding with any decision.

meta.description: Answers to the most common questions about buying or selling property with Rui Da Cruz, RE/MAX Collection.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.intro: We've gathered the questions we get asked the most. If yours isn't here, get in touch directly.

items.question: Which areas does Rui work in?
items.answer: The main focus is Parque das Nações, with a presence in Lisbon, Cascais, Porto and the Algarve too. Outside these areas, we look at it case by case.

items.question: Does Rui only work with sellers, or does he help buyers too?
items.answer: Both — full support for sellers and for buyers alike, from first contact through to the deed.

items.question: How does a first meeting work?
items.answer: No commitment required — usually a call or an in-person meeting, to understand what you're looking for (or the property you want to sell) and explain the next steps.

items.question: Does Rui work with foreign buyers / non-residents?
items.answer: Yes. For anyone buying in Portugal from abroad, we've put together a dedicated guide covering the process, timelines and typical documents.

items.question: How long does the buying or selling process usually take?
items.answer: It varies a lot depending on the property and financing involved — from the promissory contract to the deed usually takes a few weeks to a few months.

items.question: How can I schedule a viewing?
items.answer: Directly through the contact form, via WhatsApp, or by booking a call — whichever is easiest for you.
